paper.title: An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles
paper.file_name: 42_An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles.pdf
paper.research_summary: Here we extract all the meaningful device data from peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells published so far and make them available in a database. We collect data from over 42,400 photovoltaic devices with up to 100 parameters per device. We then develop open-source and accessible procedures to analyse the data, providing examples of insights that can be gleaned from the analysis of a large dataset. The database, graphics and analysis tools are made available to the community and will continue to evolve as an open-source initiative.

tasks.task_name_raw: creation of an open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells
tasks.objective: to expand the normal research cycle by collecting all perovskite solar cell data, both past and future, in one place; to make all historical data accessible and provide means to upload new experimental data; to implement interactive graphical data visualization tools that enable simple and interactive exploration, analysis and filtering
constraints: FAIR data principles (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable)
input_requirements: peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells
output_goal: free interactive web-based tools for exploration, analysis, filtering and visualization
procedures and protocols for FAIR-compliant data dissemination

evidence.text: Here we extract all the meaningful device data from peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells published so far and make them available in a database. We collect data from over 42,400 photovoltaic devices with up to 100 parameters per device. We then develop open-source and accessible procedures to analyse the data, providing examples of insights that can be gleaned from the analysis of a large dataset. The database, graphics and analysis tools are made available to the community and will continue to evolve as an open-source initiative.

stages.stage_name_raw: manual literature search and data collection
stages.stage_goal: to identify and collect all relevant peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells
stage_input: Web of Science search phrase 'perovskite solar'
stage_output: over 15,000 papers identified by end of February 2020

evidence.text: We have manually gone through every paper found in the Web of Science with the search phrase ‘perovskite solar’ up to the end of February 2020 (that is, over 15,000 papers).

stages.stage_goal: to extract device-level data from papers and format consistently according to protocol
stage_input: peer-reviewed papers with original experimental device data
stage_output: over 42,400 devices extracted with up to 100 parameters per device, consistently formatted

evidence.text: In total, we have manually extracted data for over 42,400 devices. While a few devices with extractable data will have slipped through our net, the devices in the database represent almost every device someone has thought is worth the effort to describe in detail in the peer-reviewed literature.
Once extracted, the data have been consistently formatted according to the instruction in the supporting documentation and is now freely available in the Perovskite Database.

stages.stage_name_raw: development of interactive analysis and visualization tools
stages.stage_goal: to build open-source, web-based tools enabling simple and interactive exploration, analysis, filtering and visualization without programming knowledge
stage_output: web-based tools for filtering and visualization

evidence.text: To increase the usability of the data, we have developed interactive tools for simple exploration, analysis, filtering and visualization that can be used without programming knowledge. The code base for the project is written in Python and is available at GitHub (https://github.com/Jesperkemist/perovskitedatabase), and everyone is invited to contribute and expand the scope of the project.

stages.stage_goal: to validate the database and tools by performing illustrative analyses yielding scientific insights
stage_output: example analyses including PCE evolution over time, HTL impact on Voc, bandgap-composition fitting, scalability trends, stability T80 analysis

stages.stage_name_raw: establishment of FAIR-compliant protocols and infrastructure
stages.stage_goal: to develop procedures, templates, and infrastructure ensuring long-term sustainability, trustworthiness, and community adoption
stage_output: guarantee of operational maintenance for a decade

evidence.text: The key goals of the project are to: collect all perovskite solar cell data ever published in one open-access database; develop free interactive web-based tools for simple and interactive exploration, analysis, filtering and visualization of the data; develop procedures and protocols to simplify dissemination and collection of new perovskite data according to the FAIR data principles; release an open-source code base that can be used as a blueprint for similar projects and give a few demonstrations of insights and analysis that can be easily done if all data are consistently formatted and found in one place.

To ensure the project’s longevity, we have secured support from the Helmholtz Organization in Germany, which acts as a guarantor ensuring that the web resources, that is, database, webpage and the GitHub account, will be operational and maintained for the coming decade, with an option of possible prolongation.
The database, graphics and analysis tools are made available to the community and will continue to evolve as an open-source initiative.
Once extracted, the data have been consistently formatted according to the instruction in the supporting documentation and is now freely available in the Perovskite Database.

The project has a dedicated website, www.perovskitedatabase.com that provide access to all resources. Among those are: the Perovskite Database, interactive graphics exploring the database, instructions for what is found in the database, templates and instructions for uploading new data, links to all works related to the project and so on.
